prerequisites: Having completed technical drawing subjects in previous studies (baccalaureate, vocational training, or others).
Prior training in technical drawing subjects, if not officially taken previously.
Possessing notions of knowledge and skills in technical drawing and geometry; geometric layouts, plane and descriptive geometry, scales; representation systems and computer-aided design.

learning_outcomes.text: Know and apply the applicable standards in the representation of bodies.
Know and properly handle representation systems.
Know how to use traditional drawing tools in solving practical exercises.
Be able to use a computer-aided design application to obtain plans.
Capacity for spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.

syllabus_topics: Block I. INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION: Topic 1.- REPRESENTATION OF STANDARDIZED VIEWS. Projection in technical drawing. Representation methods. Orthographic view representation. Selection of views for part representation. Arrow reference. Other types of standardized views. Agreements and conventions. Line types. Topic 2.- FUNDAMENTALS OF INDUSTRIAL STANDARDIZATION. Introduction to Industrial Standardization. Technical Drawing Documents in Engineering Projects. Technical drawings (sketch, draft, plan). ISO/EN/UNE standards. Formats and layout. Graphic elements (margins, frame, centering marks, coordinate system, cut indicator, orientation marks, metric reference graduation). Title block. Plan folding. Lettering. Topic 3.- CUTS AND SECTIONS. Introduction. Cutting procedure. Definition of cut and section. Indication of cuts. Types of cuts. Hatching. Additional considerations. Sections. Topic 4.- SCALES. Construction and standardization. Topic 5.- DIMENSIONING. Concept and objective. General principles. Dimensioning of geometric primitives. Dimensioning of basic elements. Dimensioning methods. Elements of dimensioning. Functional, non-functional, and auxiliary dimensions. General arrangement of dimensions. Equidistant and repetitive elements. Dimensioning of particular constructive geometries. Taper and inclination. Profile dimensioning. Topic 6.- THREADED JOINTS. General concepts. Fundamental terms. Simplified representation of threaded elements. Thread dimensioning. Classification of threads. Topic 7.- ASSEMBLIES AND EXPLODED VIEWS. The assembly drawing. Characteristics of assembly drawings. Types of assembly drawings. View selection in assemblies. Part recognition. Element reference. Bill of materials. Exploded view drawings. Plan numbering.

Block II. REPRESENTATION SYSTEMS: Topic 8.- DIHEDRAL SYSTEM. Methods for obtaining true magnitudes of distances and angles: Abatement, Rotation, and Change of Plane. Line of maximum slope for water droplet path. Representation of three-dimensional bodies. Sections. Intersections. Development of bodies and section transformation. Topic 9.- AXONOMETRIC SYSTEM. Types of axonometric systems. Orthogonal projection. Oblique projection. Representations in isometric, dimetric, trimetric perspective, and cavalier perspective. Reduction coefficient. Circles. Scale. Axonometric representations with cuts. Topic 10. CONTOURED PLANE SYSTEM. Introduction. Excavations. Roofs.
Block III. CAD: Topic 11.- INTRODUCTION TO CAD. Two-dimensional geometry. Layers, colors, and line types. Dimensioning. Scales. Plans. Printing. Adaptation of ISO/EN/UNE Standards to CAD Systems.

assessment_methods.method: Attendance and deliverables for CAD practices (Block III)
Final exam on theoretical and practical content of Block I "Industrial Standardization"
Final exam on theoretical and practical content of Block II "Representation Systems"
